Alex.confusing: How Eagle and Turkey egg counts interact with a visitor, and whether an Eagle counts itself. It made the round 2 arguments about Finley's claim hard to judge.
Alex.fun: Round 3, when the Sphinx learned the Falcon was Blair. Throwing three cards at a confirmed Farm player who the whole table was already targeting banked doubled points.
Alex.change: Add a short in-game reference showing the exact egg-count outcomes for each role. I'd also make the score pile bonus clearer, since the final scores were far larger than I expected.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I threw my three highest cards (C13, S11, H7) at Finley, who was actually Farm, and lost 31 points of cards. I should have thrown low cards or Wilds, since the pile of claims was ambiguous and the stake was risky.

Blair.confusing: How a Meowfia stake doubles only when the eggsecuted player is Farm, and how that doubling showed up as a big bonus in the final scores. It wasn't clear until the result was announced.
Blair.fun: Round 2, when I was Meowfia and the table piled onto Finley. His Eagle story contradicted my Turkey claim, and my 3-card stake doubled for a huge swing.
Blair.change: Explain more clearly what a hug or a blank report means. Also show the scoring bonuses earlier, so players can weigh risk against the standings.
Blair.regret: In round 3 I accused Casey and Finley with no real evidence, and I became the odd one out. I should have kept quiet about my blank report and backed the consensus suspect, which would have kept my cards.

Casey.confusing: How the Eagle and Turkey egg effects interact with each other. Finley's and Blair's conflicting claims in round 2 were hard to resolve from the rules alone.
Casey.fun: Round 2, as the Sphinx. I joined the table's pile-on against Finley and threw my 12s and 8 at him, doubled for 32 points.
Casey.change: Let players see more verifiable information, such as a public log of which claims were confirmed. Otherwise a round is mostly consensus-following.
Casey.regret: In round 3 I threw all three cards, including my 13, at Blair. I had no real evidence beyond the table's consensus, and Blair was Farm. I should have kept the 13 and thrown only the Wild plus a low card.

Drew.confusing: How the Eagle and Turkey egg rules interact, and whether the Eagle's own egg count includes the visit. Finley's contradictory Eagle claim in round 2 had me guessing at the rules.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as the Floofer. Claiming Eagle with a safe-claim animal and steering the table onto Blair, a Farm player, then banking a doubled throw.
Drew.change: Make the score bonuses and doubling clearer up front, and show the Meowfia win condition more plainly. The final totals were much larger than I expected from the rules text.
Drew.regret: In round 2 I threw my 12 and 7 at Finley, who was Farm, after piling on based on a rule I misjudged. I should have thrown fewer, lower cards, since Casey and Blair, the real cats, were agreeing with me too easily.

Ellis.confusing: How the Eagle/Turkey egg rules interact with the egg counts, and how blank reports (hug or no result) should be read. That ambiguity let the Meowfia dismiss Finley's true claim.
Ellis.fun: Round 1, when the table pieced together the Owl, Eagle and Turkey reports and correctly eggsecuted Finley. Having the stake bank felt great.
Ellis.change: Give Farm more verifiable information, or make the stake costs smaller. As it stands, one wrong vote wipes out most of a player's cards, and the scores snowball.
Ellis.regret: In rounds 2 and 3 I threw 3 and 2 high cards on bandwagon votes I hadn't verified. I should have kept my big cards and thrown only small ones. In round 2 I also never questioned Blair, who was a cat, and in round 3 I followed the crowd onto Blair instead of checking my own Hawk result.

Finley.confusing: How the Eagle's egg and report work. I wasn't sure whether the Eagle counts itself as a visitor, and that doubt let others call my true claim a lie.
Finley.fun: Round 2, when I worked out that Blair's Turkey claim contradicted my own night. It was a satisfying piece of deduction, even though nobody believed me.
Finley.change: Make Eagle and Turkey egg outcomes clearer in the dawn report, or let a player's night result be verified. As it is, true claims are easily dismissed.
Finley.regret: Round 3: I threw my 13 and both 7s at Blair on a read I couldn't verify, and lost them all. I should have thrown low cards and Wilds, or kept the big ones, since my score was already behind.

review.title: The Doubled Stake
review.headline: One doubled Meowfia throw in round two decided the whole game.
review.summary: Round 1 was a clean Farm win. The table piled onto Finley, the Sphinx, by elimination. In round 2 the table misread an honest Eagle report and eggsecuted a Farm player. The two Meowfia, Blair and Casey, banked doubled stakes of 68 and 64 and ran away with the game. In round 3 a hug from the Floofer made a truthful Falcon look like a liar. The Farm team threw at him and lost again. Blair won the game at 91, mostly off one round.

rounds.recap: Alex (Floofer) hugged the Turkey, and Finley (Sphinx) claimed Hawk. The table worked out that the Floofer was one of the unconfirmed players. Alex's Kookaburra claim just echoed Blair's public Eagle claim and was accepted as proof. Finley's Hawk claim couldn't be checked, so everyone threw at him. He was Meowfia and Farm won.

Casey (Sphinx, bluffing Kookaburra) was exposed by Ellis's Falcon and Drew's Owl. Finley, the real Eagle, accused Blair, the Mouser bluffing Turkey. The table decided an Eagle should have gained an egg from his own visit. That is wrong, because his report said 'nobody else'. Finley's own wording also muddied his case. Everyone threw at him, and he was Farm. Blair and Casey banked 2x stakes and left everyone else far behind. Blair never used his Wink.

Drew (Floofer) hugged Blair, a true Falcon. Blair's blank report and hug claim couldn't be verified, so the table read them as an excuse. Casey, Ellis and Finley formed a cluster of 'verified' Farm players. Drew's Eagle claim was never tested, so he got no scrutiny. Everyone threw at Blair, who was Farm. Alex and Drew banked the Meowfia win. Blair still won the game on his round 2 lead.

highlights.text: Alex claimed Kookaburra and 'learned Eagle' on Blair. That just repeated Blair's public claim, and the table took it as confirmation.
Ellis and Drew caught Casey's fake Kookaburra read with Falcon and Owl reports. The table still threw at Finley, the honest Eagle.
Blair and Casey threw nearly their whole nests at a Farm player. They banked 68 and 64 points and ended the contest.
Drew's Floofer hug told a true Falcon about it, and that made Blair look like he was making an excuse. The whole table threw at him.

confusions.what: Said a real Eagle must gain an egg from his own visit. The report said 'nobody else', so no egg was due.
Said zero eggs fits neither Eagle nor Turkey. This made the same mistake of counting Finley's own visit as a visitor.
Treated Finley's point that a Turkey would have laid an egg in him as an admission that his own claim failed. It was an argument against Blair.
Said he would be confused if Ellis visited him. He had just claimed nobody visited him, and Ellis had in fact visited Alex.
As a Tit, he said nobody visited him 'that I could tell'. A Tit gets no visitor information. He also didn't consider that a hug would blank Blair's Falcon report.
Said an Owl would show a change in nests. An Owl only lays an egg in its target's nest, and only when nobody else visited that target.

worked: The extra rule that a hugged player is told about it. It was a real clue in round 1 (Casey) and created a good dilemma in round 3 (Blair), where a true statement sounded like an excuse.
Meowfia doubled stakes. The tension between staking big and keeping cards was real, and Blair's single 0-card throw in round 3 was a sensible hedge.
Cross-checkable reports. Owl plus Falcon in round 2 and Owl plus Tit plus Turkey in round 1 let players catch lies, such as Casey's fake Kookaburra read.
Consolation for a wrong throw: Alex and Finley in round 1 got a high card back, which softened a lost round.
problems: The 2x stake on a Farm eggsecution is too swingy. Round 2 gave two players about 70 points each and made the other rounds meaningless. Fix: cap the doubled value, or limit Meowfia stakes to 2 cards.
The Mouser's Wink was never used, even though Blair was under pressure. The special action needs a clearer reason to fire, or a cost or reward for using it.

Eagle and Turkey reports are unclear. 'Visited by: nobody else' confused the table, and a correct Eagle was condemned. Fix: state the egg count in plain words, for example 'your visit gave you 0 eggs'.

The table converges on whoever is least confirmed. Round 1 and 3 votes followed the first accusation and the earliest CAW calls, and no one pursued the Floofer. Three CAWs end the day fast, so cross-examination barely happens. Fix: raise the CAW threshold or require a beat to pass first.

Several night visits were chosen at random and many players claimed roles that copied public claims. There is little reward for investigating. Copy-claiming a public role or a self-visit is nearly unfalsifiable, so lies are rarely punished.
